properties.description: The La Loutre project, led by Lomiko Metals in Québec, is a proposed natural flake graphite mining and processing project. The Pentagon awarded $8.35 million (USD) through the Defence Production Act to support feasibility studies and graphite processing development. Canada is contributing $4.9 million (CAD) through Natural Resources Canada to support research and pilot-scale upgrading of graphite into battery materials. Due to its high heat resistance, lightweight, and electrical conductivity, graphite is crucial for stealth technology, missiles, and armour.

The Pentagon awarded $6.4 million (USD) to Fortune Minerals for its NICO project, which targets cobalt sulfate and bismuth production. The Government of Canada is also contributing funding, providing approximately $7.5 million (CAD) to Fortune Minerals. Together, these investments are intended to advance feasibility work and project development, supporting production of cobalt and bismuth. Bismuth is used in defence electronics, lead-free bullets, and specialized alloys, while cobalt supports magnetic stealth and high-temperature components.

Proponent: Fortune Minerals
Minerals: Cobalt, gold, bismuth, copper
Funding: $6.4 million (USD)

properties.description: The Mactung project, located on the Yukon–Northwest Territories border and led by Fireweed Metals, is one of the world’s largest undeveloped deposits of tungsten, a critical mineral used in military applications. The project is being advanced with joint public funding from the United States and Canada. The Pentagon has committed approximately $15.8 million (USD) through the Defense Production Act. The Canadian government is matching this support with approximately $12.9 million (CAD) in funding. Together, these investments are intended to support feasibility studies for the required mining access road and early-stage development of the project.

The Sisson project, led by Northcliff Resources in New Brunswick, is a proposed open-pit mine targeting the critical minerals tungsten and molybdenum. The project received $15 million (USD) from the Pentagon through the Defence Production Act to support pre-construction work and feasibility updates. Canada has also committed up to $8.2 million (CAD) through Natural Resources Canada to advance engineering and development planning.

properties.minerals: Manufacturing of lithium iron phosphate cathodes
properties.description: Nano One Materials Corp. produces lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode active materials used in battery supply chains. The Pentagon awarded $12.9 million (USD) through the Defence Production Act to expand Nano One’s facilities in Québec and British Columbia. LFP cathode materials are a key component in lithium-ion batteries, with applications in both energy storage and military systems. The Government of Canada has also provided support for the project, contributing over $20 million (CAD) in funding and complementary investments.

properties.description: Electra Battery Materials’ cobalt refinery is being developed to produce cobalt sulfate—a key precursor material used in lithium-ion batteries. The Pentagon awarded $20 million (USD) through the Defence Production Act to support construction of an industrial-scale hydrometallurgical plant and establish North American production capacity. The Government of Canada has also contributed funding, providing approximately $5 million (CAD) to support related development work at the same refinery site. Cobalt sulfate produced at the facility will be used in large-capacity batteries for both commercial use and military systems.

Lithium Americas is a Vancouver-headquartered company developing the Thacker Pass lithium mine in Nevada, one of the world’s largest lithium projects. The US Department of Energy is taking a 5 per cent equity stake in Lithium Americas and a 5 per cent stake in the Thacker Pass joint venture with General Motors, alongside changes to an approximately $2.3 billion (USD) federal loan package. The project targets lithium carbonate for battery production and is expected to produce 40,000 tonnes of battery-quality lithium carbonate per year in its first phase.

properties.minerals: Copper, cobalt, zinc, lead (Ambler Road project, Alaska)
properties.description: The Pentagon is investing $35.6 million (USD) in Trilogy Metals, a Vancouver-based mining company, giving the US government an approximately 10 per cent ownership stake, with warrants to purchase an additional 7.5 per cent. The investment is intended to advance exploration and development of Trilogy’s Alaska mineral projects and support access to critical minerals outside Chinese-controlled supply chains. The Ambler Access Project is a proposed 211-mile industrial road in northwest Alaska, a district that contains copper, zinc, cobalt, silver, gold, lead and other strategic metals.

properties.description: The Strange Lake project, led by Torngat Metals, is a proposed $2 billion (USD) rare earth mining project in northern Québec and Labrador. It targets heavy rare earth elements such as dysprosium and terbium, which are used in weapons and military aircraft manufacturing. The project is majority-owned by US-based Cerberus Capital Management and is expected to supply materials to global magnet manufacturers linked to military supply chains. Canadian governments have provided political and financial support, though there are no binding requirements on how the minerals will ultimately be used.

properties.description: The Ring of Fire is a proposed mining district in northern Ontario’s James Bay Lowlands, a 5,000-km² mineral-rich region often promoted as central to Canada’s clean-tech future. It sits within the world's second largest peatland complex. While governments frame the region as a source of minerals for the green transition, the US increasingly views northern Ontario as a stable supply source for military industries. Wyloo Metals has confirmed “initial discussions” with the Pentagon about supplying minerals to the US. Several First Nations, including Neskantaga First Nation, have not consented to mining or the proposed access road.
